idiom_name: protocol conformance with hand-written forwarders; @dynamicMemberLookup for wholesale member forwarding
implementation_notes: The Swift book's own Delegation section defines delegating as handing responsibilities to another instance through a protocol, and the realization is exactly that: the wrapper declares conformance and writes each forwarded method, holding the delegate as `any Store` (an existential) or as a generic parameter. Swift has no message forwarding in pure Swift, so nothing is generated; when the delegation is wholesale - a type that forwards unknown members to a wrapped value - the `@dynamicMemberLookup` attribute with a `subscript(dynamicMember:)` gives member lookup that is resolved at runtime but still type checked. Prefer hand-written forwarding for a narrow, stable surface, and `@dynamicMemberLookup` when the wrapped API cannot be enumerated.
pitfalls: Conformance is not delegation: declaring `: Store` forces the members to exist but generates nothing, so a wrapper that only stores the delegate still implements every member or fails to compile.

`@dynamicMemberLookup` forwards member access only, through `subscript(dynamicMember:)` (key paths or member names) - it does not forward methods, and an unknown member becomes a runtime failure unless the subscript returns an optional.

Storing the delegate as `any Store` boxes it and copies value-type delegates, while storing a class delegate strongly creates retain cycles when the delegate refers back to the wrapper (the classic Cocoa `weak var delegate` rule).
